about.metaDescription: KC Technology Corporation is headquartered at Half-Mile, Limbe in the Southwest Region of Cameroon, operating Digital Marketing, Electrical Services and Real Estate.

about.intro: KC Technology Corporation operates Digital Marketing, Electrical Services and Real Estate from a single base in Limbe, Cameroon.
about.whoBody: KC Technology Corporation is a Cameroon-based company working across three departments: Digital Marketing, Electrical Services and Real Estate. Each department serves a different market, and all three operate to the same corporate standard for delivery, communication and accountability.
about.whereBody: Our head office is at Half-Mile, Limbe, in the Southwest Region of Cameroon. Real estate services extend nationwide across the country's ten regions, and digital and electrical work is delivered from our Limbe base.
about.howBody: Every engagement begins with a clear scope and a named point of contact. We quote before we start, we keep clients informed as work progresses, and we document what was delivered. Where a project needs more than one discipline, the departments coordinate under one contract rather than sending you between separate suppliers.
about.value1Body: Work is defined and quoted before it begins, so there are no surprise costs.
about.value2Body: You deal with a named contact who knows your project, not a queue.
about.value3Body: We record what was installed, published or transacted, and hand it over.
about.ctaBody: Tell us what you need and the relevant department will respond with next steps.

dm.metaDescription: Digital Marketing at KC Technology Corporation: social media, websites, SEO, advertising, content, e-commerce, training and business automation.
dm.heroHeading: Digital marketing and technology for businesses in Cameroon
dm.heroIntro: The Digital Marketing department covers the work of being found, being understood and selling online: websites, search, social media, advertising, content and the systems behind them.
dm.servicesIntro: Nine service areas. Each one is described in detail on its own page, including how the work is scoped and what you receive.
dm.servicesNote: Not sure which applies? Describe the problem and we will point you to the right one.
dm.processIntro: Every engagement follows the same shape, so you always know what is happening and what is expected of you.
dm.processStep1Body: We agree what is being delivered, by when and at what cost before any work starts. No surprise charges afterwards.
dm.processStep2Body: You get one person who knows your project and answers your questions, rather than a shared inbox.
dm.processStep3Body: Work is delivered in stages with progress reported as it goes, so problems surface early rather than at handover.
dm.processStep4Body: You receive the accounts, the files and the documentation, along with support for the questions that arise after launch.
dm.whyIntro: Digital work is easy to buy badly. These are the commitments that shape how we deliver it.
dm.why1Body: Cameroon's market works in English and French. Content is written for both audiences rather than translated from one into the other.
dm.why2Body: Domains, hosting, analytics and advertising accounts are registered in your name, so you are never locked in.
dm.why3Body: We report what happened, including when something did not work. A provider that only reports good news is not giving you a basis for decisions.
dm.why4Body: What we hand over is documented and editable by your team, so routine changes do not require a developer.
dm.faqIntro: The questions we are asked most often when a project begins.
dm.faq1Question: Do you work with small businesses?
dm.faq1Answer: Yes. Work is scoped to what you actually need rather than to a fixed package, so a single website or a focused advertising campaign is a legitimate engagement. We will say when a requested piece of work is not worth the cost.
dm.faq2Question: Can you work with both English and French customers?
dm.faq2Answer: Yes, and it is central to how we plan. Cameroon's market is bilingual, so websites, content and campaigns are prepared for both language audiences rather than assuming one.
dm.faq3Answer: Yes. Support arrangements are agreed explicitly, with what is covered and how quickly, rather than left to goodwill. Many clients start with a project and add ongoing support once they see how the work fits their team.
dm.faq4Answer: By scope, not by a published rate card. We quote after understanding the requirement, so the figure reflects the work rather than a guess made before knowing it.
dm.ctaBody: Describe the requirement and the Digital Marketing team will respond with a scope, a quote and a named contact.

el.metaDescription: Electrical Services at KC Technology Corporation: installation, solar, maintenance, automation, CCTV, equipment supply, safety inspections, industrial contracting and low/medium voltage lines.
el.heroHeading: Electrical work for homes, businesses and industry in Cameroon
el.heroIntro: The Electrical Services department covers installation, power and protection: wiring and distribution, solar and battery systems, maintenance and repair, automation and security, equipment supply, inspection, industrial contracting and distribution lines.
el.servicesIntro: Nine service areas. Each one is described in detail on its own page, including how the work is scoped, what it covers and what you receive at handover.
el.servicesNote: Not sure which applies? Describe the site and the problem, and we will point you to the right one.
el.processIntro: Electrical work is planned before it is installed, because a fault found during commissioning is cheaper than one found later. Every engagement follows the same shape.
el.processStep1Body: We assess what exists and what it will be asked to carry, then agree the scope before any work starts. Adding load to an installation that was already near its capacity is how overloading begins.
el.processStep2Body: You receive a specification and a quote for the work: equipment ratings, cable sizes, protective devices and the programme. No substitutions are made silently.
el.processStep3Body: Work is carried out to the applicable standard and tested before energising. In occupied buildings the programme is arranged around your operating hours.
el.processStep4Body: You receive the documentation of what was installed and tested: circuit schedules, device settings and test results. That record is what makes the installation maintainable.
el.whyIntro: Electrical work is easy to buy badly, and the consequences of a bad installation are not cosmetic. These are the commitments that shape how we deliver it.
el.why1Body: A tripping breaker is a symptom. We establish the cause before changing anything, so the same fault does not return next month.
el.why2Body: Counterfeit and re-marked protective devices and cable are a real problem in the market and fail in ways that are not visible until a fault occurs. Equipment is sourced from established manufacturers through traceable channels.
el.why3Body: Circuit schedules, device ratings and test results are handed over as a record, so the installation can be maintained and extended without reconstructing how it was configured.
el.why4Body: We report on the installation we inspect and we do not issue certificates we are not entitled to issue. Where something requires another body, we say so rather than substituting our report for it.
el.faqIntro: Questions that come up before a survey. If yours is not here, ask it in a quote request.
el.faq1Answer: Yes. The department serves clients across Cameroon, and the company is based in Half-Mile, Limbe in the Southwest Region. For work outside the Southwest, travel and accommodation are part of the quote rather than a surprise later.
el.faq2Answer: Often enough to give a range, but not enough to give a firm price. Photographs help us understand the installation and prepare questions. A firm quote for installation work follows a survey, because what is behind a wall or inside a distribution board changes the scope.
el.faq3Question: How long does a quote take?
el.faq3Answer: A site visit is arranged at a time that suits you, and the quote follows once the scope is agreed. Where equipment has to be ordered, the lead time is stated in the quote rather than discovered after you commit.
el.faq4Question: Do you handle both supply and installation?
el.faq4Answer: Yes. We supply equipment for our own installations and for installations delivered by others, matched to the specification rather than to what is in stock. Taking supply and installation together is what keeps the equipment consistent with the design.

checkout.contactIntro: We use these to confirm the order and reach you about delivery.
checkout.fieldEmailHint: Your order confirmation and receipt are sent here.
checkout.fieldPhoneHint: Optional, but needed for mobile money and delivery calls.
checkout.fulfillmentIntro: Choose how you would like to receive the order.
checkout.fieldDeliveryNotesHint: Optional. Access instructions or a preferred time.
checkout.paymentIntro: Choose how you would like to pay.
checkout.paymentCardHint: Visa or Mastercard. You are sent to a secure page to enter card details.
checkout.paymentMtnHint: Approve the payment on your phone.
checkout.paymentOrangeHint: Approve the payment on your phone.
checkout.paymentBankHint: We send you the account details. Your order is confirmed once the transfer is received and checked by our team.
checkout.reviewIntro: Check the details above, then place your order.
checkout.consentLabel: I confirm the details above are correct and I agree to be contacted about this order.
checkout.secureNote: Card details are entered on the payment provider's secure page. We never see or store them.
checkout.errPhone: Enter a valid phone number, or leave it blank.
checkout.errAddress: A street address and town are required for delivery.
checkout.errCity: Enter the town or city for delivery.
checkout.errConsent: Please confirm your details before placing the order.
checkout.emptyCartBody: Nothing was ordered because your cart has no items. Add something and try again.
checkout.outOfStockTitle: An item is no longer available
checkout.outOfStockBody: Another customer bought the last of {item} while you were checking out. Your card has not been charged. Adjust your cart and try again.
checkout.rateLimitedBody: Please wait a few minutes before trying again.
checkout.unconfiguredBody: The store is not connected to its database, so orders cannot be placed right now. Please contact us directly.
checkout.errorBody: Your order was not placed and you have not been charged. Please try again, or contact us if it keeps happening.
checkout.paymentFailedBody: Your order is saved and no money was taken. You can try paying again from your order page.

order.thanking: Thank you. We have your order and will be in touch about delivery.
order.awaitingPaymentBank: Your order is reserved. Transfer the total to our account and send us the reference below. We will confirm the order once the transfer arrives — this is checked by our team, not automatically.
order.awaitingPaymentOnline: Your order is saved but the payment has not completed. You can try again below.
order.bankReferenceLabel: Use this reference on your transfer
order.retryFailed: We could not start the payment again. Please contact us and quote your order reference.
order.paidBody: Your payment has been confirmed and your order is being prepared.
order.failedBody: No money was taken. You can try again below, or contact us if it keeps failing.
order.cancelledBody: This order is no longer active. Place a new order if you still need these items.
order.refundedBody: The payment for this order has been returned.
order.notFoundBody: We could not find that order, or the link has expired. If you placed an order with an account, sign in and open your order history.
order.historyIntro: Orders you have placed with KC Technology Corporation.
order.historyEmpty: You have not placed any orders yet.
order.guestNoticeBody: These orders were placed from this browser without signing in. Create an account to keep them together and track future orders.
order.signInToSeeMore: Sign in to see all your orders
order.metaDescription: The status of your KC Technology Corporation order, including payment and delivery.

consent.heading: Cookies and measurement
consent.body: We use cookies to understand how the site is used. Nothing that identifies you is sent, and measurement only starts if you allow it.
consent.analyticsHint: Counts page visits and which pages are used. No names, emails or phone numbers are sent.
consent.marketingHint: Measures the performance of our advertising. Off unless you turn it on.

adminOrders.heading: Orders
adminOrders.intro: Every order placed through the store, newest first.
adminOrders.empty: No orders have been placed yet.
adminOrders.noPayments: No payment attempt has been recorded for this order.
adminOrders.updateIntro: Only transitions the order state machine allows are offered. A status change is recorded against your account.
adminOrders.noteHint: Optional. Recorded in the order history.
adminOrders.markPaidHint: Use this only after the money has genuinely arrived, for example a bank transfer you have checked. It records the payment and marks the order paid.
adminOrders.markPaidNote: Bank transfer confirmed against our account.
adminOrders.statusInvalid: That status change is not allowed from the current state.
adminOrders.paidRecorded: The payment was recorded and the order marked paid.

adminOrders.unauthenticated: Your session has ended. Sign in again and retry.
adminOrders.unconfigured: The store is not connected to a database.
adminOrders.writeFailed: The change could not be saved. Please try again.
adminOrders.manualOnlyHint: Only a bank transfer can be confirmed manually.

adminCrm.heading: Enquiries
adminCrm.intro: Every enquiry from all three departments, in one inbox.
adminCrm.noTimeline: Nothing has been recorded against this enquiry yet.
adminCrm.updateIntro: Changes are recorded in the enquiry timeline against your account.
adminCrm.writeFailed: The change could not be saved. Please try again.
adminCrm.forbidden: Your role does not allow managing enquiries.
adminCrm.unauthenticated: Your session has ended. Sign in again and retry.
adminCrm.unconfigured: The CRM is not connected to a database.

errors.forbidden: You do not have permission to change this enquiry.
errors.not_found: That enquiry could not be found.
errors.update_failed: The change could not be saved. Try again.

adminReports.heading: Reports
adminReports.intro: What the system has actually recorded. Where nothing has been recorded, a section says so rather than showing a zero that looks like a measurement.
adminReports.salesIntro: Daily totals for orders with a confirmed payment. Unpaid orders are not counted as sales.
adminReports.salesEmpty: No confirmed payments have been recorded yet.
adminReports.inquiriesIntro: Daily enquiry volume by department and type.
adminReports.inquiriesEmpty: No enquiries have been recorded yet.
adminReports.listingsIntro: Recorded listing events by type. These are counts of traffic the system logged, not estimates.
adminReports.listingsEmpty: No listing activity has been recorded yet.
adminReports.inventoryIntro: Current stock per product, with a flag for items running low.
adminReports.pipelineIntro: Orders by status, including those not yet paid.
adminReports.pipelineEmpty: No orders have been placed yet.
adminReports.noteNoPii: These reports contain counts and amounts only. No customer names, emails or phone numbers are shown here.

adminOrder.heading: Orders
adminOrder.intro: Every order placed in the store. Filter by status, open an order to change its state or record a bank transfer.
adminOrder.detailIntro: Order detail. Confirm payment, advance the order, or cancel it.
adminOrder.empty: No orders match this filter yet.
adminOrder.tableScrollLabel: Orders table, scroll horizontally to see all columns
adminOrder.noPayments: No payment has been attempted for this order yet.
adminOrder.noteHint: Recorded on the order timeline. Visible to staff only.
adminOrder.noTransitions: This order is in a final state. Nothing further can be applied to it.
adminOrder.invalidTransition: That change is not allowed from the order's current state. Reload the page and try again.
adminOrder.forbidden: You do not have permission to change orders.
adminOrder.actionError: The change could not be saved. Please try again.
adminOrder.manualIntro: Use this only after the transfer has cleared in the business account. It marks the order paid and records a manual payment; the money is not verified by the payment provider.
adminOrder.manualCaution: This order is awaiting a bank transfer. Confirm the money has arrived before recording it.
adminOrder.manualNoteHint: For example the bank reference on the statement.
adminOrder.manualRecorded: The payment was recorded and the order is now paid.
adminOrder.manualNotApplicable: This order cannot be confirmed by hand — it has already been paid or it was not set up as a bank transfer.

adminProfile.detailsIntro: Your role is set by an administrator and is shown here for reference only.
adminProfile.nameHint: Shown on enquiries you handle and on anything you publish.

adminProfile.phoneHint: Optional. Used by colleagues and, where relevant, by customers.

adminProfile.passwordIntro: Use at least 12 characters. A longer passphrase is stronger than a short complex password.

adminSettings.heading: Settings
adminSettings.intro: Console settings and the preferences you control.
adminSettings.accountIntro: Update your name, picture and password.
adminSettings.appearanceIntro: The console language follows your account's preferred language.
adminSettings.systemIntro: The settings that affect the whole site are managed by a super administrator.
adminSettings.integrationsIntro: Translation sync and payments are configured with environment variables and are not edited here.

adminUsers.heading: Users & Roles
adminUsers.intro: Everyone with console access, and the role that governs what they can do.
adminUsers.noteBody: Changing a role is a privileged operation that must be audited; it is performed with the role-change action that writes a system log entry, not by editing this table.

adminSecurity.heading: Security
adminSecurity.intro: The controls that protect the console, and how they are enforced.
adminSecurity.authBody: Sign-in is handled by Supabase Auth. Passwords are hashed by the auth service and never stored by the application.
adminSecurity.rlsBody: Every table holding customer or internal data carries row-level security policies; the console reads and writes through those policies rather than bypassing them.
adminSecurity.uploadsBody: Uploaded files are typed by inspecting their leading bytes, not by their filename or declared type, and are stored under a path built from a fresh identifier.
adminSecurity.auditBody: Privileged changes are recorded. Super administrators can read the trail in System logs.
